adea0bf635dd806c1.summary: As of August 12, 2026: Next.js latest stable is 16.3.0 (released Aug 3, 2026), pairing with React 19.2 (npm latest react is 19.2.8); create-next-app 16.3.0 defaults to TypeScript + ESLint + Tailwind CSS v4 (@tailwindcss/postcss, no tailwind.config) + App Router + Turbopack + AGENTS.md. Tailwind's current release is 4.3.3. shadcn CLI is at 4.x with `npx shadcn init`; big 2026 shifts: unified radix-ui package (Feb), CLI v4 with presets/templates (Mar), and Base UI replacing Radix as the default primitive library for NEW projects (Jul) — Radix still fully supported via `-b radix`. Vercel Postgres is gone (migrated to Neon via Vercel Marketplace, Dec 2024–Q1 2025); for a hobby project the default pick is Neon through the Marketplace (0.5 GB, 100 CU-hrs/mo, scale-to-zero after 5 min) with Supabase (500 MB DB, pauses after 1 week idle) as the batteries-included alternative — both offer PostGIS free. Drizzle stable is drizzle-orm 0.45.2 / drizzle-kit 0.31.10 (v1.0 is at RC stage — not stable yet), with @neondatabase/serverless via drizzle-orm/neon-http as the serverless driver of choice and tsx-run seed scripts. Zod is at 4.4.3 (top-level z.email(), unified `error` param). For PWA, Next natively provides app/manifest.ts and its official guide shows a hand-rolled minimal service worker (recommended for push-only), with @serwist/next 9.5.12 as the maintained next-pwa successor for full offline precaching. Vercel Hobby: fluid compute on by default, 300s max duration (default and cap), streaming/SSE supported, stable after() from next/server for post-response work. Caching: Cache Components ("use cache" + cacheComponents: true) is the current model — opt-in in 16.3, slated to become default in a future major; unstable_cache is deprecated; revalidateTag (new SWR signature) and new updateTag are the invalidation APIs.
facts: Next.js latest stable is 16.3.0, released August 3, 2026 (verified via nextjs.org/blog/next-16-3 and registry.npmjs.org/next/latest = 16.3.0; create-next-app latest is also 16.3.0).
Next.js 16 pairs with React 19.2; npm latest react is 19.2.8; next@16.3.0 peerDependencies allow ^18.2.0 || ^19.0.0 (verified via registry.npmjs.org and nextjs.org/blog/next-16 coverage).

create-next-app recommended defaults are TypeScript, ESLint, Tailwind CSS, App Router, AGENTS.md, Turbopack enabled, import alias @/*; Biome is offered as an alternative linter (verified via nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/cli/create-next-app, lastUpdated 2026-08-10).

create-next-app's Tailwind template is Tailwind v4: its postcss.config.mjs uses @tailwindcss/postcss and there is no tailwind.config file (verified via raw.githubusercontent.com vercel/next.js canary packages/create-next-app/templates/app-tw/ts).

Tailwind CSS current version is 4.3.3 (verified via registry.npmjs.org/tailwindcss/latest); v4.2 (Feb 2026) added an official webpack plugin, 4 new color palettes, and complete logical-property utilities.

shadcn CLI package is at 4.17.0 (registry.npmjs.org/shadcn/latest); init is `npx shadcn@latest init` / `npx shadcn init`; Tailwind v4 support uses CSS variables with @theme inline, cssVariables: true default in components.json, tokens like bg-background/text-foreground, dark mode via .dark overrides, and empty tailwind config path for v4 (ui.shadcn.com/docs/tailwind-v4, /docs/theming).

shadcn 2026 changes: Feb 2026 unified radix-ui package; Mar 2026 CLI v4 (presets, --template scaffolds, --base flag, --dry-run/--diff, shadcn info/docs, registry:base/registry:font); Jul 2026 Base UI became the DEFAULT primitive library for new projects — keep Radix with `npx shadcn init -b radix`; Radix is not deprecated and all components ship for both (verified via ui.shadcn.com/docs/changelog/2026-07-base-ui-default and 2026-03-cli-v4).

Vercel Postgres was sunset: all stores were auto-migrated to Neon (Q4 2024–Q1 2025), @vercel/postgres is no longer maintained, and new projects must install a Postgres integration from the Vercel Marketplace; Neon recommends @neondatabase/serverless for new projects (verified via neon.com/docs/guides/vercel-postgres-transition-guide and vercel.com/docs/postgres).

Neon Free plan: 0.5 GB storage per project, 100 CU-hours/month per project (~400 hrs at 0.25 CU), compute scales to zero after 5 minutes idle, up to 2 CU when active, ~100 projects, 10 branches/project, 5 GB egress; exceeding storage or CU-hours suspends the project (verified via neon.com/faqs/free-plan-limits-and-quotas search results).

Supabase Free plan: 500 MB database, 1 GB file storage, 5 GB egress, 50k MAU, 2 active projects; projects PAUSE after 1 week of database inactivity and take ~30s to resume (verified via multiple 2026 pricing writeups including supabase-sourced docs).

PostGIS is available on the free tier of BOTH: Neon supports PostGIS across all plans via CREATE EXTENSION (neon.com/docs/extensions/postgis); Supabase enables PostGIS from dashboard or `create extension postgis` with no plan restriction (supabase.com/docs/guides/database/extensions/postgis).

Drizzle current stable: drizzle-orm 0.45.2 and drizzle-kit 0.31.10 (verified via registry.npmjs.org); v1.0 is NOT stable yet — 1.0.0-rc.1 exists (~June 2026) with an architecture rewrite, migration-table changes (name/applied_at columns via drizzle-kit up), and generate-time branch-conflict detection (orm.drizzle.team/docs/upgrade-v1, /docs/v0-v1-changes).

Drizzle driver guidance: use drizzle-orm/neon-http with @neondatabase/serverless for serverless (Vercel) against Neon; the WebSocket neon-serverless driver if you need sessions/interactive transactions; postgres-js or node-postgres for serverful environments (orm.drizzle.team/docs/connect-neon and neon.com/docs/guides/drizzle).

Seed pattern: a tsx-run script, e.g. package.json "db:seed": "tsx ./src/db/seed.ts" (or `node --import tsx --env-file .env`), optionally using the drizzle-seed package for generated data (orm.drizzle.team/docs/seed-overview).

Zod current version is 4.4.3 (verified via registry.npmjs.org/zod/latest). v4 changes from v3: top-level tree-shakeable formats z.email()/z.uuid()/z.url() (chained z.string().email() deprecated but still works); single `error` param replaces message/invalid_type_error/required_error/errorMap; error-map precedence flipped (schema-level error now beats parse-time contextual map); .parse/.safeParse/z.infer unchanged (zod.dev/v4/changelog).

PWA: @serwist/next is at 9.5.12 with peer next >=14.0.0 (npm registry) and is the maintained successor to next-pwa (unmaintained; requires --webpack under Next 16, while Serwist works with Turbopack). Next natively provides app/manifest.ts (MetadataRoute.Manifest); the official Next PWA guide (updated 2026-07-30) shows manifest.ts + a hand-rolled minimal service worker for push/install, points to Serwist for full offline precaching, and mentions the new experimental useOffline hook/config in 16.3 (nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/progressive-web-apps).

Vercel Hobby limits (fluid compute, which is enabled by default for new projects): max duration 300s — both default and maximum (Pro: 300s default, 800s max, 1800s extended beta); memory 2 GB/1 vCPU; request/response body max 4.5 MB; concurrency auto-scales to 30,000; Edge runtime must start responding within 25s and can stream up to 300s. Max duration includes time spent on streamed responses, i.e. SSE/streaming from route handlers is supported and counts against the cap (verified via vercel.com/docs/functions/limitations, last_updated 2026-07-01).

Post-response background work: after() from next/server is STABLE (stable since Next 15.1; formerly unstable_after) and is built on waitUntil; it works in Server Components, Server Actions, Route Handlers, and Middleware; work must still finish within maxDuration — for longer jobs Vercel docs point to Vercel Workflows (nextjs.org docs + vercel.com/docs/functions/limitations).

Caching in Next 16.x: Cache Components — the 'use cache' directive enabled by top-level `cacheComponents: true` (plus `partialPrefetching: true` in 16.3) — is the current model; the 16.3 blog states these behaviors will become the DEFAULT in a future major ('dynamic by default, no hidden or implicit caching'). unstable_cache is deprecated/replaced by 'use cache'. revalidateTag is stable but under cacheComponents requires a cacheLife profile second argument (e.g. 'max') for stale-while-revalidate; the new updateTag (Server Actions only) gives read-your-own-writes immediate expiry; the old fetch-options caching model is now documented as 'Caching (Previous Model)' (nextjs.org/blog/next-16-3, nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components, nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/unstable_cache).
adea0bf635dd806c1.recommendation: For a new production app on Vercel today (Aug 2026): scaffold with `npx create-next-app@latest` (gives next@16.3.0, react@19.2.x, tailwindcss@^4.3.3 via @tailwindcss/postcss, TypeScript, ESLint, App Router, Turbopack). Enable `cacheComponents: true` (and optionally `partialPrefetching: true`) in next.config.ts from day one and use 'use cache' + cacheTag/cacheLife + updateTag/revalidateTag — do not build on unstable_cache or fetch-option caching. UI: `npx shadcn@latest init` (shadcn CLI 4.17.0); explicitly choose your primitive base — `-b radix` if you want the mature Radix ecosystem and pre-2026 component compatibility, otherwise accept the new Base UI default. Database: provision Neon Free through the Vercel Marketplace (env vars auto-wired, PostGIS available via CREATE EXTENSION); use drizzle-orm@0.45.2 + drizzle-kit@0.31.10 with @neondatabase/serverless through drizzle-orm/neon-http (switch to the neon-serverless WebSocket driver only if you need interactive transactions); workflow: drizzle-kit generate → drizzle-kit migrate (push for prototyping), seed via `"db:seed": "tsx ./src/db/seed.ts"` (+ drizzle-seed for fake data). Pick Supabase Free instead only if you want bundled auth/storage/realtime and can tolerate the 7-day inactivity pause. Validation: zod@4.4.3 with top-level formats (z.email(), z.uuid()) and the unified `error` param in route handlers. PWA: start with native app/manifest.ts + the hand-rolled minimal service worker from the official Next PWA guide (sufficient for install + web push); adopt @serwist/next@9.5.12 only if you need real offline precaching (it is the maintained next-pwa successor and works with Turbopack). Rely on fluid compute defaults on Hobby (300s max), stream SSE from route handlers freely, and use the stable `after()` from next/server for post-response work.
risks: Vercel Hobby hard-caps function duration at 300s even with fluid compute (no 800s option), the cap INCLUDES streaming time, and request/response bodies are limited to 4.5 MB — long SSE sessions and big uploads need design workarounds.
after() work still counts against maxDuration — it is not a job queue; anything that can exceed the remaining budget needs Vercel Workflows, a cron, or an external queue.

Supabase Free pauses projects after 1 week of database inactivity (~30s wake, manual unpause) — a demo or low-traffic production app will randomly appear down; Neon Free instead suspends when you exceed 0.5 GB storage or 100 CU-hours, and scale-to-zero after 5 min idle adds cold-start latency to the first query.

drizzle-orm/neon-http has no session/interactive transaction support — code using db.transaction() with multiple round trips needs the neon-serverless WebSocket driver; also do NOT adopt drizzle 1.0.0-rc in production yet (migration-table format and kit behavior changed vs 0.x).

shadcn's July 2026 switch to Base UI as default means most tutorials, community registries, and pre-2026 component code assume Radix — mixing the two primitive bases in one app is painful; decide -b radix vs Base UI at init and stay consistent. The Feb 2026 unified radix-ui package also changed import paths from @radix-ui/react-* per-package imports.

Zod v4's flipped error-map precedence (schema-level error now wins over parse-time contextual maps) can silently change error messages when porting v3 patterns; chained formats like z.string().email() are deprecated and emit warnings.

revalidateTag's signature changes under cacheComponents (requires a cacheLife profile as second argument for SWR semantics) — copy-pasted Next 14/15 invalidation code will not behave the same; unstable_cache is deprecated in 16.
next-pwa is unmaintained and webpack-only while Next 16 defaults to Turbopack — avoid it entirely; even Serwist needs --webpack for local dev SW testing in some setups.
The old @vercel/postgres SDK is unmaintained — do not use it or tutorials built on it; use @neondatabase/serverless (or @neondatabase/vercel-postgres-compat only for legacy code).

Exact free-tier connection-count limits for Neon (per compute size) and Supabase (direct vs Supavisor pooler) were not pinned down in this pass — verify against current provider docs before choosing a pooling strategy; with Supabase + Drizzle use the transaction pooler with prepared statements disabled per Drizzle's Supabase guidance.

a98c7f30dab168588.summary: As of August 2026 the stack to build is: maplibre-gl v6 (v6.0.0 shipped 2026-07-22, latest 6.3.0 on 2026-08-10 — ESM-only, WebGL2-required, and bundler apps must call setWorkerUrl() once) wrapped with @vis.gl/react-maplibre 8.1.2 (2026-07-29; the dedicated MapLibre spin-off of react-map-gl, identical components to react-map-gl/maplibre, supports maplibre v4–v6), rendered inside a 'use client' wrapper loaded via next/dynamic ssr:false from a client component. Basemap: OpenFreeMap's Positron style (https://tiles.openfreemap.org/styles/positron) — free, keyless, no request limits, commercial use explicitly allowed, light/minimal/label-forward and fits an editorial off-white design; fallback is a self-hosted Protomaps PMTiles basemap ("white" or "light" flavor via @protomaps/basemaps) on range-request storage (Cloudflare R2 or Vercel Blob — a full planet is ~120GB so it cannot live in Vercel's /public, whose source upload cap is 100MB Hobby / 1GB Pro, but a low-zoom or regional `pmtiles extract` can). CARTO basemaps are now Enterprise-license-only for commercial use and MapLibre demo tiles are demo/CI-only, so both are out. Route animation: @turf/great-circle 7.4.0 to generate arcs (returns MultiLineString across the antimeridian), drawn as a GeoJSON source with lineMetrics:true and a line-gradient whose ['line-progress'] step threshold is advanced in requestAnimationFrame — MapLibre has no line-trim-offset (still an open spec proposal), and line-gradient can't combine with line-dasharray, so gradient-head animation (or per-frame setData slicing) is the way; sequential reveal = one gradient-animated segment at a time with staggered start times. Geolocation→locality: BigDataCloud's free client-side reverse-geocode API (no key, no rate limit, client-side fair-use only) with coordinates rounded before the call; Nominatim only as a 1 req/s attributed fallback.
facts: maplibre-gl latest is 6.3.0, published 2026-08-10; v6.0.0 was published 2026-07-22 and v5.24.0 (last v5 minor) 2026-04-23 — verified via npm registry (npm view maplibre-gl time/dist-tags).

MapLibre GL JS v6 is ESM-only (UMD bundles discontinued, bundle is maplibre-gl.mjs), requires WebGL2 (WebGL1 removed, TS target ES2022), and bundler users must call setWorkerUrl() once before rendering a map — verified via the GitHub v6.0.0 release notes and the official v5-to-v6 migration guide (maplibre.org/maplibre-gl-js/docs/guides/v5-to-v6-migration-guide/); the webpack/Next.js pattern is setWorkerUrl(new URL('maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl-worker.mjs', import.meta.url).toString()).

@vis.gl/react-maplibre latest is 8.1.2 (published 2026-07-29), peerDependency maplibre-gl >=4.0.0, described as 'React components for Maplibre GL JS'; react-map-gl latest is also 8.1.2 published the same minute (same monorepo, lockstep versions) — verified via npm registry.

react-map-gl v8 (Feb 2025) split into react-map-gl/mapbox, react-map-gl/maplibre, and react-map-gl/mapbox-legacy endpoints; the docs' What's New page states v8.1 explicitly supports MapLibre GL JS v4, v5, and v6, and that MapLibre v6 apps using a bundler must configure the worker before rendering — verified at visgl.github.io/react-map-gl/docs/whats-new and /docs/get-started.

@vis.gl/react-maplibre is the dedicated MapLibre package spun off from react-map-gl because maintaining Mapbox+MapLibre in one API became complex; it exists to enable MapLibre-specific functionality — verified at visgl.github.io/react-maplibre/docs.

OpenFreeMap: free public instance with no limits on map views or requests, no registration/API keys, commercial use explicitly permitted; required attribution 'OpenFreeMap © OpenMapTiles Data from OpenStreetMap' is auto-added when using MapLibre; no SLA (donation-funded, run by Zsolt Ero on dedicated servers); style URLs are https://tiles.openfreemap.org/styles/{positron|bright|liberty|dark|fiord} — verified at openfreemap.org and openfreemap.org/quick_start/.

CARTO basemaps (basemaps.cartocdn.com) are 'available exclusively with an Enterprise license' for commercial use; free access only via the non-profit grants program — verified at docs.carto.com/faqs/carto-basemaps, so they are NOT safe for commercial production without a contract.

MapLibre demo tiles (demotiles.maplibre.org) are 'demo vector tiles and map style for web, helloworld and CI tests' hosted on GitHub Pages; official MapLibre docs tell users to provide their own tiles or use a provider (Stadia/MapTiler) for production — verified via github.com/maplibre/demotiles and maplibre.org docs.

Protomaps full-planet PMTiles basemap is ~120GB (z0–15); each zoom level roughly doubles file size; smaller files via `pmtiles extract` with region bounds and/or --maxzoom — verified at docs.protomaps.com/basemaps/downloads. Style flavors from @protomaps/basemaps (namedFlavor()): light, dark, white, grayscale, black — 'white' and 'grayscale' are the data-viz/minimal flavors — verified at docs.protomaps.com/basemaps/flavors.

PMTiles hosting requires HTTP Range request support plus CORS (Access-Control-Allow-Origin and Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Range); Protomaps' cloud-storage docs recommend Cloudflare R2/S3/GCS/Azure/Bunny/B2/Supabase and note GitHub Pages works under 1GB; Vercel is not in their docs, but Vercel Blob serves byte-range requests and the maplibre-org agent-skills doc states Netlify/Vercel static hosting accepts .pmtiles with Range support — verified at docs.protomaps.com/pmtiles/cloud-storage and github.com/maplibre/maplibre-agent-skills.

Vercel deployment source-file upload limit is 100 MB (Hobby) / 1 GB (Pro), 15,000 files max — verified at vercel.com/docs/limits (page dated 2026-08-03) — so a planet PMTiles cannot ship inside the deployment; use Blob/R2 for anything big.

@turf/great-circle and @turf/turf are at 7.4.0 (turf last modified 2026-08-03) — verified via npm registry. greatCircle(start, end, {npoints, offset, properties}) returns a LineString, or a MultiLineString split at the antimeridian — verified via turfjs.org/docs and the package README. Known regression: 'greatCircle broken for routes crossing the antimeridian in v7.3.2+' (Turfjs/turf issue #3030) — test your longest east-west routes.

MapLibre line-gradient works only on GeoJSON sources with lineMetrics: true; line-gradient cannot be combined with line-dasharray (maplibre-gl-js issue #5082); line-trim-offset does NOT exist in MapLibre — it is an open proposal (maplibre-style-spec issue #1360, referencing Mapbox's property); official examples exist for 'animate a line' (per-frame setData) and 'animate a point along a route', and the ml-line-animation library implements the sliding line-gradient-head technique — all verified via maplibre.org examples and GitHub.

In Next.js App Router, next/dynamic with ssr: false is not allowed in Server Components — the dynamic import must live inside a 'use client' component (wrapper-component pattern) — verified via nextjs.org lazy-loading guide and multiple 2025–2026 write-ups on the maplibre/leaflet + App Router pattern.

iOS Safari WebGL: resizing an on-screen WebGL canvas leaks memory (WebKit bug 219780; process killed near ~1.25GB), MapLibre maps have crashed on iOS after repeated loads (maplibre-gl-js issue #7667) and HiDPI/oversized sprites significantly increase memory and crash mobile devices (issue #4153) — verified via webkit.org bugzilla and GitHub issues.

BigDataCloud's client-side reverse-geocode API (api.bigdatacloud.net/data/reverse-geocode-client) is free with no API key, no sign-up, and no rate limits; returns country/state/city/locality/postcode; falls back to IP-based locality when called without coordinates; fair-use terms require calls from the end-user's device for that device's current location (no server-side or batch/stored-coordinate use); they state coordinates are processed and discarded — verified at bigdatacloud.com/free-api and their docs/blog.

Nominatim public API policy (operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/nominatim/): absolute maximum 1 request/second, valid User-Agent or Referer required, OSM/ODbL attribution required, no systematic/grid reverse queries, and apps whose primary function is geocoding must self-host — verified via the OSMF policy page.
a98c7f30dab168588.recommendation: Install: `maplibre-gl@^6.3.0`, `@vis.gl/react-maplibre@^8.1.2` (import { Map, Source, Layer } from '@vis.gl/react-maplibre' — or the byte-identical `react-map-gl@^8.1.2` with the 'react-map-gl/maplibre' entry; pick @vis.gl/react-maplibre as the forward-looking dedicated package), and `@turf/great-circle@^7.4.0`. If you want zero migration risk this month, `maplibre-gl@5.24.0` is the conservative pin (v6 is only 3 weeks old and the wrapper supports >=4); otherwise take v6 and add the one-time `import { setWorkerUrl } from 'maplibre-gl'; setWorkerUrl(new URL('maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl-worker.mjs', import.meta.url).toString())` plus `import 'maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl.css'` in your map client component. Structure: server page → small 'use client' wrapper that does `dynamic(() => import('./route-map'), { ssr: false })` → map component. Basemap: mapStyle="https://tiles.openfreemap.org/styles/positron" (light, minimal, label-forward, keyless, commercial-OK, attribution auto-injected); fallback: self-hosted Protomaps PMTiles (pmtiles extract with --maxzoom 8–10 world build, or your corridor regions) on Cloudflare R2 free tier (or Vercel Blob — both serve Range requests) styled with namedFlavor('white') from @protomaps/basemaps + the `pmtiles` protocol package; wire the fallback by swapping the style prop on a tile-load 'error' event. Routes: build arcs with turf greatCircle (npoints ~128; handle MultiLineString antimeridian output; test against turf issue #3030), put all arcs in one GeoJSON source with lineMetrics: true, draw a thin base line (line-width ~1–1.5, low-opacity) plus an animated overlay using line-gradient with a ['step', ['line-progress'], color, t, 'rgba(0,0,0,0)'] head threshold `t` advanced per-route in a single requestAnimationFrame loop (setPaintProperty per frame); stagger each route's start time for the sequential reveal (do NOT plan on line-trim-offset — MapLibre doesn't have it; do NOT combine line-gradient with line-dasharray — unsupported). Reverse geocoding: call https://api.bigdatacloud.net/data/reverse-geocode-client?latitude=..&longitude=..&localityLanguage=en directly from the browser after navigator.geolocation, rounding coords to 2 decimals (~1.1 km) before the call, and persist only the returned city/locality string — free, keyless, no rate limit, and compliant with their client-side fair-use terms; keep Nominatim (1 req/s + User-Agent + OSM attribution) only as a low-volume fallback.
risks: maplibre-gl v6 is 3 weeks old (v6.0.0 2026-07-22): ESM-only and WebGL2-only. Forgetting the one-time setWorkerUrl() call in a bundler app is the classic breakage (map silently fails/worker 404). WebGL2 excludes pre-2022 browsers; add a maplibregl.supported-style check or fall back to a static image.

@vis.gl/react-maplibre 8.1.2's peer range (maplibre-gl >=4.0.0) accepts v6, and the docs claim v4/v5/v6 support, but v6-specific bugs in the wrapper may still surface — if you hit one, downgrading only maplibre-gl to 5.24.0 is a clean escape hatch.

OpenFreeMap has no SLA — it is a donation-funded single-maintainer service (reliable reputation since 2024, but plan the Protomaps self-hosted fallback and make the style URL a config value so you can swap without a deploy).

CARTO's Positron style via basemaps.cartocdn.com is widely copy-pasted in tutorials but is Enterprise-only for commercial use in 2026 — do not ship it. MapLibre demo tiles are demo/CI-only. Both look free and are not.

PMTiles on Vercel: nothing over ~100MB (Hobby) / 1GB (Pro) can go in /public; use Vercel Blob or Cloudflare R2, set CORS (Allow-Origin + Allow-Headers: Range), and remember every tile fetch is a billable ranged GET on most object stores (R2 has free egress, making it the cheapest fallback host).

turf greatCircle antimeridian regression in v7.3.2+ (Turfjs/turf #3030): routes crossing the dateline (e.g., Shanghai→LA) may render broken. Test those routes; if broken, pin an earlier @turf/great-circle or split arcs manually.

line-gradient constraints: requires lineMetrics:true (larger tile/source memory), cannot coexist with line-dasharray on the same layer, and per-frame setPaintProperty on many separate layers is expensive — keep routes in one source, one overlay layer if possible, and drive all animations from a single rAF loop; pause the loop when the tab/section is hidden (document.visibilitychange + IntersectionObserver).

Tab layouts: a map initialized inside a display:none container sizes to 0. MapLibre's trackResize/ResizeObserver usually recovers, but call map.resize() when the tab becomes visible, and never mount two live maps in parallel tabs on mobile.

Mobile Safari: WebKit leaks memory on WebGL canvas resize (bug 219780, kill near ~1.25GB) and MapLibre has documented iOS crash issues (#7667, #4153). Mitigate: single map instance, cap pixelRatio (e.g. Math.min(devicePixelRatio, 2)), modest sprite/image sizes, avoid orientation-driven resize churn, and fully map.remove() on unmount.

BigDataCloud free endpoint is client-side-only by its fair-use terms — never proxy it through your API routes or batch-geocode stored coordinates (that requires their paid server API). Its 'free because we correlate coords with requesting IP' model may matter for your privacy page wording. Nominatim at 1 req/s with mandatory attribution is not a production-scale primary.
Privacy goal (no precise coords stored): round to 2 decimals before the reverse-geocode call and store only the locality string — the API sees a ~1km-fuzzed point and your DB never holds the raw fix.

a982ae933f11175d1.summary: For a v1 provenance app, four sources can go live today, free and legally: Open Food Facts (API v3 is current/recommended — live-tested product-by-barcode with brands/categories/origins/manufacturing_places/ecoscore fields; ODbL with mandatory attribution + share-alike; mandatory custom User-Agent; low rate limits of 15 read req/min/IP), USDA FoodData Central (free api.data.gov key, CC0, live-tested UPC lookup via /foods/search with the gtinUpc field on Branded foods), openFDA food/drug enforcement (free, live-tested at api.fda.gov/food/enforcement.json; recalls match by brand/firm text and UPCs embedded as free text in code_info/product_description), and UPCitemdb's keyless trial tier (live-tested, 100 lookups/day) for generic non-food UPCs. The OFF siblings (Products/Beauty/Pet Food Facts) share the exact same API but have tiny catalogs (~44k/~73k/~15k products), so they're a cheap add-on, not a non-food solution. GS1 prefix→company resolution has NO free API in Aug 2026: GEPIR was retired 2023-12-31, replaced by Verified by GS1 / GS1 US Company Database (free web UI, 30 searches/day, no API; programmatic access needs GS1 US Data Hub from $500/yr) — mock adapter. US bill-of-lading data is effectively commercial-only (ImportYeti API is paid; Panjiva/ImportGenius/Datamyne enterprise; CBP AMS raw data was ruled unavailable via FOIA in 2023 and is officially sold via paid CBP subscription) — mock adapter. Corporate disclosures (Oatly sustainability reports, Tony's Chocolonely FAIR report 2024/25, Patagonia factory/farm/mill lists, plus Open Supply Hub's CC-BY-SA facility database) all exist with URLs and work as static seed evidence.
facts: Open Food Facts: API v3 (latest v3.6) is marked 'Current — recommended for all new integrations'; v2 is deprecated but still supported. Verified at https://openfoodfacts.github.io/openfoodfacts-server/api/ (fetched 2026-08-12).

Open Food Facts product-by-barcode endpoint live-tested: GET https://world.openfoodfacts.org/api/v3/product/3017624010701?fields=code,product_name,brands,categories,origins,manufacturing_places,ecoscore_grade,image_front_url returned status:success with brands='Ferrero', ecoscore_grade='d', and image_front_url on images.openfoodfacts.org (path pattern /images/products/301/762/401/0701/front_en.{rev}.{size}.jpg). v2 form is /api/v2/product/{barcode} (docs tutorial). origins and manufacturing_places are real fields but were empty even for Nutella — sparsely populated.

Open Food Facts rate limits, verified in raw docs HTML: 15 req/min/IP for all read product queries, 10 req/min/IP for search queries, no limit on writes; HTTP 503 when exceeded; for mobile apps where requests come from end users, limits apply per user. A custom User-Agent in the form 'AppName/Version (contact@email)' is mandatory; reads need no other auth.

Open Food Facts licensing (verified at https://world.openfoodfacts.org/terms-of-use): database under ODbL, contents under DBCL, photos under CC BY-SA. Reuse requires attribution to Open Food Facts with a link to https://openfoodfacts.org (or the product page), license mention, and share-alike on any derived database; photo license does not clear third-party trademark/design rights on the packaging shown.

Open Beauty Facts / Open Products Facts / Open Pet Food Facts share the same Product Opener API shape — live-tested /api/v2/product/{barcode} and /api/v2/search on world.openbeautyfacts.org, world.openproductsfacts.org, world.openpetfoodfacts.org on 2026-08-12. Total catalog sizes from the search API: Beauty ~72,921, Products ~44,093, Pet Food ~14,976 — i.e., very thin coverage for arbitrary non-food UPCs.

USDA FoodData Central (verified at https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/api-guide/ and live call): free API key via api.data.gov signup (/api-key-signup); default 1,000 req/hour/IP; DEMO_KEY limited to 30 req/hr and 50 req/day; base URL https://api.nal.usda.gov/fdc/v1/; data is public domain CC0 1.0.

FDC UPC lookup live-tested 2026-08-12: GET https://api.nal.usda.gov/fdc/v1/foods/search?api_key=DEMO_KEY&query=041303001165&dataType=Branded returned exactly 1 hit with gtinUpc='041303001165', brandOwner='Supervalu, Inc.', full ingredients. There is no dedicated barcode endpoint — you put the GTIN in the general 'query' param (works best with dataType=Branded) and confirm the match against the returned gtinUpc field. Note FDC stores 12-digit UPC without the leading EAN-13 zero.

openFDA enforcement live-tested 2026-08-12: GET https://api.fda.gov/food/enforcement.json?search=product_description:chocolate&limit=1 returned records last_updated 2026-08-05 with fields recalling_firm, product_description, code_info, distribution_pattern, classification, status. UPCs appear only as free text inside product_description/code_info (example in live result: 'UPC 6 55974 89001 2' — with spaces), so UPC matching requires text search with formatting variants; brand/firm matching uses recalling_firm or product_description. Drug recalls live at /drug/enforcement.json with the same shape (searchable-fields page confirmed the same field set).

openFDA limits (verified at https://open.fda.gov/apis/authentication/): no key = 240 req/min and 1,000 req/day per IP; free API key = 240 req/min and 120,000 req/day per key; key passed as api_key query param or basic-auth username; HTTPS required.

GS1: GEPIR was discontinued/replaced by Verified by GS1 as of 31 December 2023 (Wikipedia GEPIR + GS1 US pages via search). The GS1 US Company Database (gs1us.org/tools/gs1-company-database-gepir, fetched 2026-08-12) offers a free web UI with up to 30 searches/day by GTIN, GS1 Company Prefix, GLN, or company name, returning licensee (company) info and basic product data for 2M+ member companies in 120+ countries — but explicitly no API at that tier. Programmatic access requires GS1 US Data Hub (from $500/yr) plus its API add-on; a 60-day API trial exists limited to 1,000 calls per API (store.gs1us.org). So prefix→company CAN be resolved legally and free, but only manually/low-volume via the web UI.

US bills of lading: the Data Liberation Project's FOIA request for CBP bill-of-lading data (submitted 2023-04-27) was rejected the next day — CBP says manifest records are 'unavailable via FOIA'; the official channel is a paid CBP data subscription of AMS vessel manifest data under 19 CFR 103.31 (verified at data-liberation-project.org/requests/cbp-bills-of-lading/ and ecfr.gov). No open bulk BoL dataset exists; OEC sells BoL bulk downloads commercially (oec.world).

ImportYeti: website remains free to browse ('free forever' tier; login required after ~25 page views/IP); API access exists only on paid plans (~$50/month billed annually per SoftwareAdvice 2026 profile); importyeti.com/yeti-api returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch, consistent with anti-bot posture — assume ToS forbids scraping. Panjiva (S&P Global), ImportGenius, and Descartes Datamyne are enterprise commercial products with no free API tiers (verified via 2026 review/comparison pages).

UPCitemdb live-tested 2026-08-12: GET https://api.upcitemdb.com/prod/trial/lookup?upc=0885909950805 works with no signup/key and returned full product data (title, brand, model, EAN/UPC). Free 'Explorer' plan = 100 combined requests/day (search capped at 40/day); paid Dev plan = 20,000 lookups + 2,000 searches/day (upcitemdb.com docs via search). Barcode Lookup (barcodelookup.com/api): paid, from $99/month, free test account for evaluation. Go-UPC (go-upc.com/plans/api): paid, from $19.95/month, trial key on request.

Corporate seed evidence verified to exist: Oatly sustainability reports — 2024 update PDF at https://a.storyblok.com/f/107921/x/cbdb92c917/oatly-sustainability-update-2024.pdf and 2025 Sustainability Report via https://investors.oatly.com (includes oat sourcing detail, e.g., Finland/Sweden/UK sourcing shifts). Tony's Chocolonely annual FAIR report 2024/25 at https://tonyschocolonely.com/pages/annual-fair-report-2024-2025 (Open Chain sourcing model, cooperatives expanded 11→19 in Ghana/Côte d'Ivoire). Patagonia publishes factory/farm/mill supplier disclosure pages (https://www.patagonia.com/working-with-factories-farms-mills/ and regional equivalents confirmed in search index; patagonia.com was serving an outage page to fetches on 2026-08-12 so page contents could not be re-read directly).

Open Supply Hub (bonus source, verified at info.opensupplyhub.org): all facility data including OS IDs is licensed CC BY-SA 4.0; a free account can search and download up to 5,000 production locations at no cost; the REST API requires a trial signup or paid subscription. Useful as the structured home of brand supplier lists (apparel brands like Patagonia contribute lists there).
a982ae933f11175d1.recommendation: GO LIVE in v1 with five adapters: (1) Open Food Facts as the primary GTIN resolver — use GET https://world.openfoodfacts.org/api/v2/product/{barcode} or /api/v3/product/{barcode} (v3 recommended; note v3 nests data under 'product' with a 'result.id' status while v2 uses 'status'), request fields=product_name,brands,categories_tags,origins,origins_tags,manufacturing_places,ecoscore_grade,ecoscore_data,image_front_url,countries_tags; send User-Agent 'YourApp/1.0 (contact@yourdomain)'; cache aggressively to stay under 15 read req/min/IP. Reuse the same adapter with base hosts world.openproductsfacts.org / world.openbeautyfacts.org / world.openpetfoodfacts.org as fallbacks. (2) USDA FoodData Central with a free api.data.gov key: GET https://api.nal.usda.gov/fdc/v1/foods/search?query={gtin}&dataType=Branded, then verify response foods[].gtinUpc equals the scanned code (strip/add leading zero for EAN-13↔UPC-12); gives brandOwner (the actual company, great provenance signal) and ingredients under CC0. (3) openFDA recalls with a free key: GET https://api.fda.gov/food/enforcement.json?search=... and /drug/enforcement.json — match by recalling_firm/brand tokens plus a fuzzy text search of the UPC (try raw digits and space-grouped variants) against code_info and product_description. (4) UPCitemdb trial endpoint GET https://api.upcitemdb.com/prod/trial/lookup?upc={gtin} for non-food UPCs (100/day free — fine for a demo; upgrade to their Dev plan or Go-UPC at $19.95/mo when volume grows). (5) A static 'curated evidence' adapter seeded with the verified corporate disclosures (Oatly sustainability reports, Tony's FAIR report 2024/25, Patagonia supplier pages) plus a one-time free download of up to 5,000 Open Supply Hub locations (CC BY-SA 4.0). Build MOCK adapters for: GS1 company-prefix resolution (model the interface on GS1 US Data Hub's licensee lookup; no free API — the free GS1 web UI at gs1us.org allows only 30 manual searches/day, which you can use to hand-seed fixtures legally) and for bills of lading / customs shipments (model on ImportYeti/Panjiva record shape: shipper, consignee, HS code, port, date; all real sources are paid, and raw CBP AMS data is not FOIA-able). Attribution requirements to ship in v1: an 'Open Food Facts' credit with link + ODbL/CC-BY-SA notice wherever OFF data/images appear (and accept share-alike if you build a derived database), the CC0 citation line for FoodData Central ('U.S. Department of Agriculture… FoodData Central, fdc.nal.usda.gov'), openFDA's disclaimer that results are unvalidated and not for medical decisions, and CC BY-SA 4.0 attribution for any Open Supply Hub records.
risks: Open Food Facts rate limits are low (15 read req/min/IP, 10 search req/min; HTTP 503 then possible IP ban) — a server-side proxy funneling all users through one IP will hit them fast; either call OFF from the client (limits then apply per user) or cache/replicate via their bulk exports.

ODbL share-alike is viral: if you mix OFF data into your own product database and publicly use it, the derived database must be offered under ODbL too — keep OFF data in a separable layer if your evidence DB must stay proprietary; OFF product photos (CC BY-SA) also carry third-party trademark/packaging rights.

OFF provenance fields (origins, manufacturing_places) are crowd-sourced and sparse — empty even for Nutella in the live test; treat them as optional evidence, never guaranteed. Also the Eco-Score was rebranded 'Green-Score' in late 2024/2025 and the API is migrating field names (ecoscore_* still worked live, but watch for environmental_score_* aliases in v3).

FDC branded-food records lag reality (live test hit a record publishedDate 2022) and gtinUpc is stored as 12-digit UPC — normalize leading zeros both ways or lookups will silently miss; DEMO_KEY (30/hr, 50/day) is for exploration only.

openFDA recall matching by UPC is inherently fuzzy: UPCs live as inconsistently formatted free text ('UPC 6 55974 89001 2') inside code_info/product_description, so expect false negatives; FDA also warns recall status is frozen after publication — don't present it as live recall status.

GS1: there is no free programmatic prefix→company path in Aug 2026; scraping Verified by GS1 / GS1 US Company Database would violate their terms and both sites actively block bots (gs1.org returned 403 to fetches). Budget $500+/yr for Data Hub + API add-on if this must go live, or keep it mocked.

Bills of lading: all usable sources are commercial (ImportYeti API paid ~$50/mo annual; Panjiva/ImportGenius/Datamyne enterprise-priced); CBP rejected FOIA for the raw AMS data (Apr 2023) and sells it via subscription instead — also note shippers can request confidentiality under 19 CFR 103.31, so even paid BoL data has systematic gaps.

UPCitemdb trial tier (100 req/day, ~search 40/day, burst-limited) is demo-grade only and its ToS require rate compliance; Barcode Lookup jumps straight to $99/mo — plan the paid path before launch traffic.

patagonia.com was serving an outage/anti-bot page during verification (2026-08-12); the factory-list pages are confirmed to exist via the search index and regional mirrors, but re-verify exact URLs before hardcoding them as seed evidence; prefer pulling their list from Open Supply Hub (CC BY-SA) for a stable, structured copy.

Coverage gap: for arbitrary non-food UPCs the open ecosystem is weak (Open Products Facts ~44k items total), so v1 should set expectations that non-food scans often resolve via UPCitemdb (title/brand only) with no provenance evidence attached.

a8d1f39805d781095.summary: As of August 2026, the native BarcodeDetector API is still unusable on iOS: Safari (including 26.x, latest 26.5) ships it only behind the disabled-by-default "Shape Detection API" experimental flag, and even that path is reported broken on iOS since iOS 18. Android Chrome (83+) and Samsung Internet (13+) support it natively via Google Play Services ML Kit, but it returns zero supported formats on GMS-free devices, and desktop Chrome/Edge only actually work on macOS/ChromeOS. The clear fallback winner is the `barcode-detector` ponyfill (v3.2.1, published 2026-07-12, wrapping ZXing-C++ WASM via zxing-wasm 3.1.1) — it decodes UPC-A/EAN-13/EAN-8/QR/DataMatrix with the exact BarcodeDetector API shape; html5-qrcode is abandoned (last publish April 2023) and quagga2 is 1D-only. For camera work on iOS Safari you get HTTPS-only getUserMedia, required `playsinline`, automatic (but uncontrollable) continuous autofocus, plus `zoom` (Safari 17.0+) and `torch` (~17.4/17.5+) constraints; the big pitfall is standalone/home-screen PWAs re-prompting for camera permission on every launch. Haptics: navigator.vibrate works on Android Chrome only, and the iOS `<input type="checkbox" switch>` haptic hack was patched by Apple in iOS 26.5, so there is currently no legitimate programmatic web haptic on up-to-date iPhones. For GS1 parsing, `@valentynb/gs1-parser` 2.0.0 (May 2026) is the maintained AI element-string parser, with `digital-link.js` 1.4.3 for GS1 Digital Link URIs.
facts: BarcodeDetector on iOS Safari: NOT available in any released iOS version as of Aug 2026. MDN BCD (via unpkg @mdn/browser-compat-data) shows safari/safari_ios support only behind the 'Shape Detection API' preference flag since Safari 17, disabled by default; caniuse.com/mdn-api_barcodedetector shows all Safari versions through 26.5 as 'Disabled by default'; not mentioned in Safari 26.0-26.5 release notes (webkit.org blog 17333, 17938); WebKit bug 281848 reports the flagged Shape Detection API broken on iOS since iOS 18.

BarcodeDetector on Android Chrome: supported since Chrome 83 (MDN BCD: chrome_android version_added 83); Samsung Internet since 13.0. Implementation delegates to Google Play Services ML Kit; per the Chromium Intent-to-Ship and spec design, getSupportedFormats() returns an empty set on devices without GMS to signal a polyfill is needed.

BarcodeDetector on desktop: MDN BCD marks Chrome 88+ partial_implementation with note 'Supported on ChromeOS and macOS only' (Chrome 83-87 macOS only; before Chrome 113 it silently failed on macOS 13+, crbug 40245611); Edge mirrors Chrome (partial); Firefox: not supported (bugzil.la/1553738 open). caniuse global usage: ~49.5% supported + ~26.9% partial.

npm registry (registry.npmjs.org, queried 2026-08-12): barcode-detector latest 3.2.1 published 2026-07-12 (depends on zxing-wasm pinned 3.1.1); zxing-wasm latest 3.1.2 published 2026-07-18 (ZXing-C++ WASM, ES/CJS with types); @zxing/browser latest 0.2.1 published 2026-07-06 (revived after ~2-year gap since 0.1.5 in May 2024; on @zxing/library 0.23.0, Apr 2026 — TS port of the old Java ZXing core); html5-qrcode latest 2.3.8 published 2023-04-15 (unmaintained 3+ years); @ericblade/quagga2 latest 1.12.1 published 2025-12-20 (maintained, but 1D-only: EAN/UPC/Code128 etc.; no DataMatrix, QR only via external plugin reader).

barcode-detector ponyfill (github.com/Sec-ant/barcode-detector README): supports upc_a, ean_13, ean_8, qr_code, data_matrix (full ZXing-C++ format list); import subpaths 'barcode-detector/ponyfill' (no global) and 'barcode-detector/polyfill' (registers global if absent; old 'pure'/'side-effects' subpaths deprecated); WASM is fetched at runtime from jsDelivr by default and can be self-hosted via prepareZXingModule({overrides:{locateFile}}).

getUserMedia on iOS Safari: secure context (HTTPS) required; <video> needs playsinline (plus muted+autoplay for autoplay); facingMode:'environment' works; continuous autofocus is automatic OS behavior but focusMode/focusDistance constraints are NOT exposed on iOS (Chrome Android only — verified via Dynamsoft camera-focus article and Apple dev forums thread 776460 on iOS 18 lens switching).

Torch and zoom ARE now available on iOS Safari: WebKit blog 'WebKit Features in Safari 17.0' explicitly lists 'exposing zoom in MediaTrackCapabilities'; whiteBalanceMode added in Safari 17.4 cycle (STP 181 release notes); Safari 17.5 release notes (Apple developer JSON) fix 'camera pausing occasionally when torch is enabled' proving torch shipped by 17.4/17.5; Safari 18.4 release notes fix stale getSettings() values for torch and whiteBalanceMode.

iOS standalone PWA camera pitfall (verified via STRICH KB article 29, WebKit bugs 215884/185448, Apple forums thread 788518): camera permission is NOT persisted for home-screen web apps — users are re-prompted every launch (and on hash change); in-browser Safari users can persist via aA menu > Website Settings > Camera: Allow; the only global workaround (Settings > Safari > Camera: Allow) is a blanket grant.

navigator.vibrate (MDN BCD): Chrome/Chrome Android since 32 (requires user gesture since Chrome 60, returns false otherwise; blocked in cross-origin iframes since 55); Safari and iOS Safari: never implemented (version_added: false); Firefox desktop REMOVED support in Firefox 129.

iOS web haptics hack: the <input type='checkbox' switch> (attribute shipped Safari 17.4) label-click trick triggered the Taptic Engine and worked on iOS 17.4-26.4, but Apple patched it in iOS 26.5 — programmatic JS haptics no longer fire (verified via web-haptics-polyfill docs/demo page and rapidtoolset.com iOS haptics tester: 'Programmatic iOS haptics work on iOS 17.4 to 26.4. Apple patched the underlying behavior in iOS 26.5'). Real user-initiated toggles of a visible switch still produce a system haptic.

PWA on iOS 26 (verified via mjtsai.com 'Web Apps in iOS 26', mobiloud/magicbell 2026 guides): every site added to the Home Screen now opens as a web app by DEFAULT, even without a manifest; the Add-to-Home-Screen sheet has an 'Open as Web App' toggle. Manifest display/name honored when present; a 180x180 apple-touch-icon remains the reliable icon path; service workers (supported since iOS 11.3) are NOT required for install; push notifications still require iOS 16.4+ plus home-screen install.

GS1 parsers on npm (registry queried 2026-08-12): @valentynb/gs1-parser 2.0.0 published 2026-05-04 (actively maintained TypeScript parser of GS1 element strings/AIs incl. (01) GTIN, (10) lot, (17) expiry; FNC1/GS-aware; modern fork of PeterBrockfeld/BarcodeParser); gs1-barcode-parser-mod 1.0.7 (2024-09); digital-link.js 1.4.3 (2024-06-03, GS1 Digital Link URI SDK); bark-js stale since 2022; gs1js dead since 2016.
a8d1f39805d781095.recommendation: Use the ponyfill-always approach rather than native-with-fallback: install `barcode-detector@3.2.1` (which pins `zxing-wasm@3.1.1` internally) and import `{ BarcodeDetector }` from `"barcode-detector/ponyfill"` unconditionally on every platform. Rationale: native BarcodeDetector is iOS-absent, desktop-partial (macOS/ChromeOS only), GMS-dependent on Android, and has per-device format gaps — the ponyfill gives one consistent, W3C-shaped API and identical decode behavior everywhere, and ZXing-C++ WASM decodes UPC-A/EAN-13/EAN-8/QR/GS1-DataMatrix well from live `<video>` frames (construct with `formats: ["upc_a","ean_13","ean_8","qr_code","data_matrix"]` and call `detect(videoEl)` on a rAF/interval loop). If you insist on native-first, gate it on `('BarcodeDetector' in globalThis) && (await BarcodeDetector.getSupportedFormats())` containing ALL required formats, else fall back to the same ponyfill — never assume the native object works just because it exists. Self-host the .wasm (it defaults to jsDelivr CDN) via `prepareZXingModule({ overrides: { locateFile } })` from `"barcode-detector/ponyfill"`. For GS1 parse, feed the raw decoded string (ZXing preserves the GS/0x1D separators) into `@valentynb/gs1-parser@2.0.0` to extract AI (01) GTIN, (10) lot, (17) expiry; add `digital-link.js@1.4.3` only if you must handle GS1 Digital Link URLs. Camera: `getUserMedia({ video: { facingMode: { ideal: "environment" }, width: { ideal: 1920 } } })`, HTTPS only, `<video playsinline muted autoplay>`; offer torch/zoom buttons feature-detected via `track.getCapabilities()` (works on Android Chrome, and on iOS Safari 17.4+/17.0+ respectively). Haptics: `navigator.vibrate(50)` behind a capability check for Android; on iOS treat haptics as unavailable (the switch hack died in iOS 26.5) and use a visual flash + short WebAudio beep as scan feedback. PWA: ship a manifest (standalone, icons) plus a 180x180 apple-touch-icon, but strongly consider steering iOS users to run the scanner in Safari (browser tab) rather than the installed standalone app, because standalone mode re-prompts for camera permission on every launch.
risks: Native BarcodeDetector on Android silently degrades: on devices without Google Play Services (and in some WebViews) the object exists but getSupportedFormats() is empty — any native-first path must check formats, not just presence, or scanning silently never detects.

iOS standalone PWA camera permission is NOT persisted (WebKit bug 215884 still open): users get the camera prompt on every app launch and on hash-change navigations — a scan-heavy app installed to the home screen will feel broken; plan UX around it or avoid forcing standalone.

The iOS switch-haptic hack is dead on current iOS (patched 26.5) but still works on 17.4-26.4 — if you ship a library like ios-haptics or web-haptics-polyfill, behavior will be inconsistent across the installed base and may be further locked down; do not build UX that depends on haptic confirmation.

barcode-detector fetches its ~1MB .wasm from jsDelivr by default — a CSP, offline PWA cache, or CDN outage breaks scanning; self-host the wasm and precache it in the service worker. Also keep barcode-detector and any direct zxing-wasm usage version-aligned (3.2.1 pins zxing-wasm exactly 3.1.1; mixing 3.1.2 directly can double-load different wasm binaries).

iOS Safari lacks focusMode/focusDistance: close-up 1D barcodes can hunt focus, and iOS 17/18 may auto-switch between back lenses mid-stream (Apple forums thread 776460); requesting ~1080p and using the zoom constraint (Safari 17+) instead of physically moving closer mitigates macro-lens switching.

Torch on iOS only arrived around Safari 17.4/17.5 and had bugs through 18.4 (stale getSettings, camera pausing) — feature-detect via track.getCapabilities().torch and expect older iOS 16/17.0-17.3 devices to lack it.

@zxing/browser was just revived (0.2.x, 2026) after two dormant years and sits on the aging TS port of Java ZXing — riskier maintenance bet than the Sec-ant/zxing-wasm stack; html5-qrcode (last publish 2023-04) should be treated as abandoned despite its download numbers; quagga2 cannot do DataMatrix at all.

iOS Safari getUserMedia stops the stream when the page is backgrounded or the screen locks, and only one active camera stream is allowed — rebuild the stream on visibilitychange/pageshow or scans fail after app switching.

GS1 separator handling: UPC/EAN scans need no parsing, but GS1 DataMatrix AI parsing requires the invisible GS (0x1D) character to survive the decode path — verify your ZXing text-mode settings end-to-end with a real (17)-expiry (10)-lot code, since variable-length AI (10) parses wrongly if GS chars are stripped.
Firefox removed navigator.vibrate in 129 — do not assume vibrate() based on 'not Safari'; always feature-detect.
